title: Maas Studio TV: A Cast-Only Guest Home
description: A native Android TV home screen for a guest apartment: cast from your phone, find local tips, and scan Wi-Fi or check-in codes without a TV login.
body:
A guest TV should explain itself, not ask for another login.

I built and installed a native Android TV home screen for Maas Studio, a guest apartment in the Netherlands. Instead of opening a wall of streaming-app tiles, the TV welcomes guests, explains how to cast from their own phone, and puts the practical information for their stay within reach.

## A home screen, not another streaming app

The main screen combines a large welcome message with three casting instructions. The Cast symbol appears only where it is needed: the final step. Language controls, FAQs, regional tips, settings, Wi-Fi settings and inputs have visible rounded outlines so guests can tell what they can select with the remote.

English, German and Dutch are available. A manual language choice stays in memory for the session and survives opening an information page or waking the home screen. It is not saved as a guest preference.

The home screen's small QR card alternates between Wi-Fi and check-in every ten seconds. Selecting it enlarges the code currently on screen.

## Practical information without leaving the TV

The FAQ reader contains complete answers and the original reference photos for heating, air conditioning, lighting and laundry. Text and images share one scrollable reading area, so the remote can reach the end of an answer as well as the photos below it.

A separate catalogue presents twelve regional recommendations. Each detail page keeps its photograph, full description and location-specific Google Maps QR together. The check-in link connects to the separate [MaasStudio Guest Check-in project](/projects/maasstudio/); the TV itself does not collect registration documents.

## A quiet screen between interactions

After inactivity, the home screen gives way to landscape photography and a large localized welcome. Two equally sized cards keep Wi-Fi details and a short check-in reminder readable, with opaque QR codes that are not blurred into the background.

The idle presentation rotates languages independently of a guest's manual home-screen choice. Waking it returns to that choice. The photo animation remains slow, and the home-screen timers pause when the application is not visible.

## Built against the actual screen

This is a native Android application, with a browser preview for comparing layout and behaviour. I checked native rendering at 720p and 1080p, then inspected the installed home and idle screens on the physical TV. The latest release passed 87 native tests and the browser checks; the alternating QR codes were also observed on the device.

The work was mostly about the details that disappear in a polished mockup: making clickable controls obvious before focus, keeping both QR cards aligned, preserving full answers when images are added, and decoding recommendation photos at the resolution their cover crop actually needs.

## What is shipped, and what is not claimed

The native home screen is installed and set as the TV's default Home. It contains no streaming-app tiles or TV-side guest account flow. That is a property of this launcher, not a claim that the operating system or casting services process no data.

Phone-based QR scans, real casting with picture and sound, HDMI handover, standby and longer idle sessions remain separate hardware acceptance checks. The operational source and assets are backed up privately; Wi-Fi credentials and operational QR images are not published here.
